title: Manual FMA from regression calibration fits
text: Frequentist model averaging (FMA) ameras() fits association model dose realization, computes AIC weights across realization specific fits, samples fitted normal approximation realization proportion weight. Usually, simplest approach let ameras() directly methods = "FMA". large datasets many dose realizations, however, can useful split work smaller jobs. vignette shows basic manual workflow: fit separate RC models individual dose realizations, save fitted summaries desired, compute FMA weights samples across realization-specific fits. example uses Gaussian model keep code compact avoid extra parameter transformations. idea applies families, provided every realization fit formula structure, family, dose-response model, starting values, optimizer settings, transformation arguments.

title: Manual FMA from regression calibration fits
text: first helper mirrors convergence Hessian screen used built-FMA. second helper fits one standard regression calibration model single dose realization. returned list keeps pieces needed model averaging: coefficient estimates, variance-covariance matrix, maximized log-likelihood, AIC. Fit model separately dose realization. large analyses, call can run separate R sessions submitted separate jobs. Save summaries job read back model averaging.
code: data(data, package = "ameras") dosevars <- paste0("V", 1:10) passes_fma_screen <- function(rc) {   hessian <- rc$optim$hessian    if (is.null(hessian) || rc$optim$convergence != 0) {     return(FALSE)   }    isTRUE(det(hessian) != 0 &&     rcond(hessian) > .Machine$double.eps &&     all(eigen(hessian)$values > 0)) }  fit_rc_realization <- function(dosevar, data) {   formula <- stats::as.formula(     paste0("Y.gaussian ~ dose(", dosevar, ") + X1 + X2")   )    fit <- ameras(formula, data = data, family = "gaussian")   rc <- fit$RC    list(     dosevar = dosevar,     coefficients = rc$coefficients,     vcov = rc$vcov,     loglik = rc$loglik,     AIC = -2 * rc$loglik + 2 * length(rc$coefficients),     include = passes_fma_screen(rc)   ) } rc_summaries <- lapply(dosevars, fit_rc_realization, data = data) dir.create("fma-fits", showWarnings = FALSE)  for (dosevar in dosevars) {   fit_summary <- fit_rc_realization(dosevar, data = data)   saveRDS(fit_summary, file = file.path("fma-fits", paste0(dosevar, ".rds"))) }  fit_files <- file.path("fma-fits", paste0(dosevars, ".rds")) rc_summaries <- lapply(fit_files, readRDS)

title: Manual FMA from regression calibration fits
text: next helper performs model averaging step. first drops realization pass FMA screen. computes stabilized AIC weights, allocates MFMA samples across realizations, draws realization-specific normal approximation, summarizes combined samples. interval calculation shown equal-tailed percentile interval, matching confint(..., type = "percentile") FMA. ameras also supports highest posterior density intervals FMA type = "hpd", implemented manual helper. diagnostics table reports many realization-specific fits removed convergence/Hessian screen many passed screen received zero FMA samples chosen MFMA. weights show realization-specific fits contributed samples integer allocation MFMA.
code: assemble_manual_fma <- function(rc_summaries, MFMA = 100000) {   n_total <- length(rc_summaries)   valid <- vapply(rc_summaries, function(x) isTRUE(x$include), logical(1))   n_screen_excluded <- sum(!valid)    if (!any(valid)) {     stop("No realization-specific fits are available for FMA.")   }    original_indices <- which(valid)   rc_summaries <- rc_summaries[valid]    AIC <- vapply(rc_summaries, `[[`, numeric(1), "AIC")   weights <- exp(-0.5 * (AIC - min(AIC)))   weights <- weights / sum(weights)    allocated_samples <- round(weights * MFMA)   keep <- allocated_samples > 0   n_weight_excluded <- sum(!keep)    if (!any(keep)) {     stop("No realizations received FMA samples. Increase MFMA.")   }    rc_summaries <- rc_summaries[keep]   original_indices <- original_indices[keep]   weights <- weights[keep]   allocated_samples <- allocated_samples[keep]   names(weights) <- vapply(rc_summaries, `[[`, character(1), "dosevar")   diagnostics <- data.frame(     stage = c(       "total realization-specific fits",       "excluded by convergence/Hessian screen",       "excluded after zero-sample allocation",       "included in manual FMA"     ),     realizations = c(       n_total,       n_screen_excluded,       n_weight_excluded,       length(original_indices)     ),     row.names = NULL   )    samples <- do.call(     "rbind",     Map(       function(fit, n) {         mvtnorm::rmvnorm(n = n, mean = fit$coefficients, sigma = fit$vcov)       },       rc_summaries,       allocated_samples     )   )    samples <- as.data.frame(samples)   names(samples) <- names(rc_summaries[[1]]$coefficients)    coefficients <- colMeans(samples)   se <- apply(samples, 2, stats::sd)   percentile_CI <- t(     apply(samples, 2, stats::quantile, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))   )   colnames(percentile_CI) <- c("lower", "upper")    list(     coefficients = coefficients,     SE = se,     percentile_CI = percentile_CI,     vcov = stats::var(samples),     weights = weights,     samples = samples,     included.realizations = original_indices,     included.samples = nrow(samples),     diagnostics = diagnostics   ) } set.seed(100) manual_fma <- assemble_manual_fma(rc_summaries, MFMA = 100000) manual_fma$diagnostics #>                                    stage realizations #> 1 code: transform1 <- function(params, index.t=1:length(params), lowlimit=rep(0,length(index.t)),                         boundcheck=FALSE, boundtol=1e-3, ...){      if(length(index.t)!=length(lowlimit))      stop("Length mismatch between index.t and lowlimit")   if(any(!(index.t %in% 1:length(params))))      stop("Incorrect indices for transformation specified")   params[index.t] <- exp(params[index.t]) + lowlimit   if(boundcheck){     if(any(params[index.t]-lowlimit < boundtol))        warning(paste0("WARNING: one or multiple parameter estimates within ", boundtol, " of          lower bounds. Try different bounds or starting values."))   }   return(params) }  transform1.jacobian <- function(params, index.t=1:length(params), ...){    if(any(!(index.t %in% 1:length(params))))      stop("Incorrect indices for transformation specified")   grad <- rep(1, length(params))   grad[index.t] <- exp(params[index.t])   if(length(params)>1){     return(diag(grad))   } else{     return(matrix(grad))   } }

title: Analyze Multiple Exposure Realizations — ameras
text: Fit regression models accounting exposure uncertainty using multiple Monte Carlo exposure realizations. Six outcome model families supported. first Gaussian family continuous outcomes, $$Y_i \sim N(\mu_i, \sigma^2),$$ \(\mu_i = \alpha_0 + \bm X_i^T \bm \alpha +\beta_1 D_i+\beta_2 D_i^2 + \bm M_i^T \bm \beta_{m1}D_i + \bm M_i^T \bm \beta_{m2}D_i^2\). \(\bm X_i\) covariates, \(D_i\) exposure measurement error, \(\bm M_i\) binary effect modifiers. quadratic exposure terms effect modification optional. non-Gaussian families, three relative risk models main exposure supported, usual exponential \(RR_i=\exp(\beta_1 D_i+\beta_2 D_i^2+ \bm M_i^T \bm \beta_{m1}D_i + \bm M_i^T \bm \beta_{m2} D_i^2)\) linear excess relative risk (ERR) model \(RR_i= 1+\beta_1 D_i+\beta_2 D_i^2 + \bm M_i^T \bm \beta_{m1}D_i + \bm M_i^T \bm \beta_{m2}D_i^2\), quadratic effect modification terms optional. Finally, linear-exponential relative risk model \(RR_i= 1+(\beta_1 + \bm{M}_i^T \bm{\beta}_{m1}) D_i \exp\{(\beta_2+  \bm{M}_i^T \bm{\beta}_{m2})D_i\}\) supported. second supported family logistic regression binary outcomes, probabilities $$p_i/(1-p_i)=RR_i\exp(\alpha_0+\bm X_i^T \bm \alpha).$$ Third Poisson regression counts, $$Y_i \sim \text{Poisson}(\mu_i),$$ \(\mu_i=RR_i \exp(\alpha_0 +\bm X_i^T \bm  \alpha)\times \text{offset}_i\) optional offset. Fourth proportional hazards regression time--event data, hazard function $$h(t) = h_0(t)RR_i\exp(\bm X_i^T \bm \alpha),$$ \(h_0\) baseline hazard. Fifth multinomial logistic regression categorical outcome \(Z>2\) outcome categories, last category referent category (.e., \(\alpha_{0,Z}=\bm \alpha_{Z}=\beta_{1,Z}=\beta_{2,Z}=\bm \beta_{m1,Z} = \bm \beta_{m2,Z}=0\)): $$P(Y_i=z)=RR_i\exp(\alpha_{0,z}+\bm X_i^T \bm \alpha_{z})/\{1+\sum_{s=1}^{Z-1} RR_i\exp(\alpha_{0,s}+\bm X_i^T \bm \alpha_{s})\}$$ Sixth conditional logistic regression matched case control data, $$P\left(Y_i = 1, Y_k = 0 \forall k \neq \bigg| \sum_{\\mathcal{R}} Y_i = 1\right) = RR_i\exp(\bm X_i^T \bm \alpha)/\{\sum_{k \\mathcal{R}}RR_k\exp(\bm X_k^T \bm \alpha)\},$$ \(\mathcal{R}\) matched set corresponding individual \(\). Methods include regression calibration (Carroll et al. 2006 doi:10.1201/9781420010138 ), extended regression calibration (Little et al. 2023 doi:10.1038/s41598-023-42283-y ), Monte Carlo maximum likelihood (Stayner et al. 2007 doi:10.1667/RR0677.1 ), frequentist model averaging (Kwon et al. 2023 doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0290498 ), Bayesian model averaging (Kwon et al. 2016 doi:10.1002/sim.6635 ).
